chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sukuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: When one of you prays in an open land, let him place before himself something like the rear part of a saddle. If he does not find that, then a stone; if he does not find that, then an arrow; and if he does not find that, then let him draw a line on the ground before himself.

key_terms.فَلْيَخُطَّ: then let him draw a line
key_terms.مِثْلَ مُؤَخِّرَةِ الرَّحْلِ: something like the rear part of a saddle, used here as a prayer barrier

ai.seo_question: What should a person place in front of themselves when praying in an open area?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a ruling on placing a sutrah-like barrier in front of a person performing salat in open land. It shows the recommended practical alternatives, beginning with an object of notable height and ending with drawing a line on the ground when nothing else is available.
